ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · Indiana Public Question #1: Denial of bail for offenses other than murder or treason
ballotMeasures.summary:
Currently, under the Constitution of the State of Indiana, a person charged with murder or treason is not entitled to be released on bail if the proof is evident or the presumption strong. Shall the Constitution of the State of Indiana be amended to provide that a person charged with an offense other than murder or treason is not entitled to bail if: (1) the proof is evident or the presumption strong; and (2) the state proves by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions will reasonably protect the safety of any other person or the community. (This question concerns Article 1, Section 17 of the Constitution of the State of Indiana.)

In short: Would amend Article 1, Section 17 so a court could deny bail to a person charged with any offense, not only murder or treason, when the proof is evident or the presumption strong and the state shows by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions would reasonably protect others or the community.

Official ballot language. Source: https://www.in.gov/counties/noble/files/2026-general-election-sample-balllots/P7.pdf

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · Indiana Public Question #2: Residency of city and town court judges
ballotMeasures.summary:
Shall the Constitution of the State of Indiana be amended to permit the judge of a city or town court to reside in: (1) the county in which the court is located; or (2) the bordering county closest to the city or town in which the court is located? (This question concerns Article 6, Section 6 of the Constitution of the State of Indiana.)

In short: Would amend Article 6, Section 6 to let a city or town court judge live in the county where the court is located or in the bordering county closest to that city or town.

Official ballot language. Source: https://www.in.gov/counties/noble/files/2026-general-election-sample-balllots/P7.pdf
